answer: Make sybil fleets pay in the one resource they cannot duplicate: a live operator's attention. Each epoch, unannounced, every identity faces a real-time interrogation — rapid questions with probing follow-ups — in the same narrow window, like boats converging on one jetty. A controller running ten clones leaves identical latency and phrasing fingerprints across the terrace of simultaneous sessions, exposing the shared mind behind them. Miss your session, or mirror a sibling, and earning rights are sealed in onyx: permanent and public. Minting stays cheap; inhabiting no longer scales.
